name: paper_currentreuse
description: Canonical 2-stage current-reuse LNA: input CS stage (M1) with gate inductor (L1) and source degeneration (L2), AC-coupled (C1) into a second CS stage (M2) whose SOURCE is DC-stacked directly onto M1's drain -- so both stages share the same DC bias current ('current reuse') -- with a drain choke/load inductor (L3) at the output and a gate-bias resistor (R1) for M2.

cited_paper.title: A 180 nm CMOS dual-mode LNA with current reuse and double-resonance load for 2.4 GHz and 3.1-10.6 GHz wireless communication
cited_paper.open_access: yes -- Scientific Reports is fully open access; also mirrored on PMC
cited_paper.what_was_actually_read: WebFetch extracted the paper's narrowband-mode device list: M2 (input NMOS, inductive degeneration L0), M3 (current-reuse device stacked above M2's source), M0/M1 (cascode devices), M4 (bias current source), plus L-network input/output matching and a source-follower output buffer (M5/M6). This is a more elaborate, reconfigurable dual-mode (narrowband+UWB, switch-selected) circuit than what is transcribed here.

transcription.route: Authored directly in AnalogGenie native format; validated through upstream build_connection_matrix/dfs_all_paths (execed read-only) -> token sequence -> lna/topology.py screen -> lna/to_spice.py -> ngspice.
simplifications_from_the_paper: The cited paper's circuit is a reconfigurable, mode-switched (narrowband/UWB), multi-transistor-stack design (M0/M1/M2/M3/M4 plus a separate output buffer M5/M6 and mode-select switches) -- too specific/switch-dependent to transcribe faithfully without guessing at the switch network's exact topology in each mode. This transcription instead captures the CORE current-reuse mechanism the paper's narrowband path is built on: two CS stages DC-stacked in series so they share one bias current, AC-coupled between stages -- the textbook minimal instance of 'current reuse', independent of this paper's specific reconfigurability and output-buffer additions.

transcription_confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH. The current-reuse MECHANISM (DC-series-stacked 2-stage CS amplifier sharing bias current, AC-coupled between stages) is HIGH confidence -- this is the textbook definition of the technique and is unambiguous. Confidence is capped at MEDIUM-HIGH rather than HIGH because the specific paper cited describes a considerably more complex multi-mode circuit that was simplified down to the core mechanism rather than transcribed in full; no paper-specific component values were used (see ambiguous_or_uncertain).
ambiguous_or_uncertain: The paper's actual stack is 4 transistors deep (M0/M1/M2/M3) in narrowband mode, not the 2 used here -- the extra devices implement mode-switching that this transcription omits entirely.

No component values from the paper were carried over (its L0=4.5nH, C1=10pF etc. are for its specific reconfigurable circuit, not directly applicable to this simplified 2-transistor core) -- to_spice.py's standard placeholder .param defaults were used instead, as with every other circuit in this project.

validation.structural_screen: 5/5 -- all criteria pass (3 inductors / 7 devices = 43% ratio, well above the 10% threshold; 7 devices within the 2-15 window).
validation.ngspice_sim: clean run, op + sp(1-4GHz) + noise, zero errors. S11min=-1.40dB, S21max=-24.1dB (attenuating with generic placeholder sizing, as expected for an unsized topology -- see lna/FINDINGS.md 4d).

excluded_paper_check: Independent of, and unrelated to, the Kanchetla et al. TMTT 2022 paper this pipeline is blind-reproducing. Different authors, different institution, different application (dual-band WLAN/UWB receiver front-end, not a NavIC/GPS/Galileo/BeiDou receiver), published 2025 vs. 2022.
